html:
Prompt history, grouped recall and inline completion

Prompt recall reuses retained text. It does not restore a previous task's authority, attachments, Gateway selection or execution state. The history owner records text and usage, the browser groups similar prompts, and completion inserts a chosen string into the current editor. Submission remains an explicit action using that editor's current state.

The history-to-editor path

flowchart TD Record[Explicit history record or submission-owner call] --> Service[RuntimeControlsService history helpers] Service --> Settings[Shared settings history object] Settings --> API[GET prompt-history] API --> Desktop[Desktop shell history and usage view] API --> Mobile[Shared completion loader used by mobile] Desktop --> Recall[Grouped recall dialog] Desktop --> Complete[Per-input inline completion] Mobile --> Complete Recall --> Text[Exact retained source text] Complete --> Text Text --> Draft[Current editor text and draft callback] Draft --> Submit[Later explicit submission with current authority]

RuntimeControlsService owns history normalization and recording. core.py exposes GET and POST /api/agent/prompt-history. prompt_recall.js contains matching/grouping helpers and the dialog. prompt_autocomplete.js owns ghost text, the Complete action and per-input completion lifecycle.

The namespace is prompt_history, with its current value under key history. It is shared UI history rather than a conversation-specific journal. The current bound is 100 distinct retained strings. Storage trims outer whitespace and deduplicates exact text, preserving case and internal whitespace. Browser grouping uses a separate normalized identity and can combine distinct stored spellings.

Recording, counts and persistence

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Record route or submission owner participant History as History service participant Settings as Settings repository Caller->>History: Record prompt text History->>History: Convert to string and trim edges alt Blank after trimming History->>Settings: Read normalized history Settings-->>History: Stored history History-->>Caller: Normalized entries without a write else Nonblank History->>Settings: Read legacy-compatible fallback History->>Settings: Atomic update of history key Settings->>History: Current history object or absent value History->>History: Normalize current value, using legacy fallback if absent History->>History: Move exact text to newest position and increment count History->>History: Keep newest 100 entries and their counts History-->>Settings: Replacement history object Settings-->>History: Updated history object History-->>Caller: Retained entry list end

The POST schema requires a string of 1–24,000 characters and forbids extra fields. A whitespace-only value can pass that length check but becomes a read-only operation after trimming. History reads accept both the current nested object and older top-level settings. They normalize results without rewriting storage. Missing or invalid usage counts become one; Python booleans are not accepted as integer counts. Counts for evicted text are removed with the text.

Recording updates order and count in one settings transaction. Active Controller settings use the shared RAM repository's atomic update; standalone settings use BEGIN IMMEDIATE. The callback sees the current value inside that transaction, so concurrent records do not independently overwrite one another's counts. Checkpoint/recovery belongs to the Controller state owner.

The desktop shell in app.js loads server history with a request-generation check and merges local entries that arrived during the read. A failed read preserves usable tab history. The mobile composer resource initializer configures the shared completion loader instead. That loader merges supplied strings with locally remembered prompts, honors a positive server limit and keeps its successful promise for the page lifetime; failures clear the promise for a later focus-triggered retry. Neither strategy fetches a model to suggest text.

Similarity groups and exact source text

Browser normalization trims, collapses whitespace and lowercases with the en-US locale for matching. uniquePrompts walks newest first and retains the newest original string for each normalized identity. Display and insertion use that original string. Grouping considers only the newest 100 supplied history entries.

flowchart TD Input[Newest 100 supplied entries] --> Unique[Newest original string per normalized identity] Unique --> Features[Unicode code-point length and unique three-character sequences] Features --> Candidate[Visit candidate in newest-first order] Candidate --> Groups[Try existing groups in order] Groups --> Pair{Candidate matches every member?} Pair -->|Yes| Append[Append to first compatible group] Pair -->|No compatible group| New[Create group headed by candidate] Append --> Next[Continue with next candidate] New --> Next Rule[Pair rule: both at least 12 code points, length ratio at least 0.65, overlap at least 0.60] -.-> Pair Next -->|More entries| Candidate Next -->|Exhausted| Result[Newest-first groups with original text]

Pair overlap is the intersection divided by the union of the two sets of three-character sequences, known as Jaccard similarity. Repeated sequences do not carry extra weight. Length uses Unicode code points, so a surrogate pair counts as one character. Every member of a group must match the candidate; a chain of partially similar prompts cannot merge incompatible endpoints. This is a deterministic text comparison, independent of semantic model inference.

Group search matches a normalized literal substring against any variant and returns the matching member indices. It preserves group chronology and displays at most 20 groups by default. A group preview can therefore show its newer Windows variant while a search for Linux selects the matching older variant in its detail panel. The separate exported flat search() helper ranks exact matches, prefixes and substrings; the grouped dialog uses chronology instead of that ranking.

Background work, navigation and cache

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Dialog participant Group as Cooperative grouping task User->>Dialog: Open or receive changed history Dialog->>Dialog: Compare exact bounded history snapshot alt Completed cache matches Dialog->>Dialog: Render cached groups else New snapshot Dialog->>Group: Abort replaced task and start grouping Dialog-->>User: Immediately show individual recent prompts Group->>Group: Yield initially and after roughly 8 ms of work opt User inserts text or closes before grouping finishes User->>Dialog: Close dialog Dialog->>Dialog: Clear visible details and restore input focus Note over Dialog,Group: Current grouping may continue to warm the cache end Group-->>Dialog: Groups, cancellation or error alt Current request succeeded Dialog->>Dialog: Retain groups and completed cache Dialog-->>User: Refresh visible rows only if dialog is open else Current request failed without cancellation Dialog->>Dialog: Keep individual prompts without caching failed groups Dialog-->>User: Explain grouping failure if dialog is open else Aborted or replaced Dialog->>Dialog: Ignore obsolete completion end end

Grouping caches fingerprints by normalized text and prunes entries absent from the new bounded snapshot. It yields to the event loop after roughly 8 ms of work and checks its abort signal between slices. A changed history aborts the previous task. Closing the dialog alone lets current work finish and warm its cache. On a grouping failure, individual recent prompts remain available with an explanatory message.

Existing rows stay usable while the server history refreshes or grouping proceeds. The list's busy accessibility state is set only when there are no groups to use. Regrouping tries to preserve the selected original variant, even if it moved into a different group. Usage labels update without rebuilding selection. Counts are summed by normalized identity, honoring saved exact-text counts and treating legacy entries as one use. Inserting a recalled prompt does not itself record another use.

The dialog opens through Recall or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+H when no other dialog is open. It is unavailable while answering an interaction or steering from the main composer. Search and variant lists expose selected/active options. Enter in search opens a group's variants; Enter in the variant list keeps the choice highlighted. Only Use prompt inserts text. Back restores the group-list scroll position on narrow layouts, and viewport changes repair focus when a control becomes hidden. Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to the composer.

The recall controller is mounted for the page lifetime. Its public controls are update, open and delegated completion keydown; it does not expose a disposal method for its dialog or document shortcut. Transient reply inputs use the separate completion controller's cleanup described below.

Inline completion and keyboard priority

sequenceDiagram participant Input participant Complete as Input completion controller participant History as Supplied history reader Input->>Complete: Input or selection update Complete->>Complete: Check focused end-caret prefix and editor gates Complete->>Complete: Schedule 250 ms idle render Note over Input,Complete: Repeated updates for the same value keep the existing timer Complete->>History: Find newest longer literal prefix match History-->>Complete: Original string or no match Complete-->>Input: Ghost text and accessible availability message alt Tab or Complete action Input->>Complete: Explicit completion request Complete->>Complete: Recheck current prefix, visibility and length Complete-->>Input: Set exact retained text through owner callback Note over Input,Complete: Text insertion does not submit a message else Escape or changed eligibility Input->>Complete: Dismiss or move caret/change scope Complete-->>Input: Clear ghost and retain current text end

Completion requires at least three non-whitespace prefix characters and a collapsed caret at the end of the input. It matches case-insensitively against a longer retained string, preserving literal spacing and newlines rather than using the grouping normalization. Slash commands, composition, disabled/read-only/inert inputs and hidden layout prevent completion. The owning editor disables completion while its resource picker is open; a completed @ reference can still be part of a history prefix.

There is a current limitation at that boundary: selecting a parameter through the palette marks its token completed in that palette instance, but manually typing @name can leave an unmatched resource query open and suppress history completion. The selected browser case expecting that manually typed query to close does not pass in this checkout and also fails at the resumed a7507d15 baseline. The completion matcher itself accepts literal @ prefixes; the open-picker gate prevents it from rendering in this case.

Rendering rejects a suggestion beyond the input's maximum length. It mirrors input typography and scrolling into a text-only ghost and exposes a Complete button and status message. Tab can flush the idle delay immediately; with no suggestion it retains normal focus traversal. Escape suppresses completion for the current value until editing makes it eligible again. Modified keys and IME remain ordinary input. Accepting calls the owner's text setter, preserving explicit submission.

Each input has at most one controller in a WeakMap. Disposal cancels its timer and resize frame, aborts listeners, removes its completion tools and unregisters that input. The surrounding view owns its input and ghost/status elements. The instruction editor guide shows how that lifetime fits transient reply fields and resource-picker priority.

Evidence and limits

Deterministic Node tests cover similarity thresholds, Unicode, pairwise grouping, bounded history, cancellation, fingerprint reuse, chronological search, literal completion and counts. Isolated grouped-recall browser scenarios cover variant selection, background regrouping, cache warming, history races, usage updates, narrow layouts and insertion restrictions. Settings history tests cover legacy reads, exact-text usage, concurrent updates, reload and the 100-entry bound.

The selected completion browser scenarios use an isolated localhost application with fake services to exercise ghost text, caret/dismissal behavior, delayed history and resource-picker priority. They do not run live model or Gateway workloads. Five selected cases pass; the manually typed parameter-prefix case fails at the palette-visibility expectation described above. The two JavaScript implementation modules are reviewed in full; history persistence and shell integration are reviewed only at the linked boundaries. These scenarios do not certify every caller's submission accounting or physical-device behavior.
